theory.title: App Router Architecture
theory.content:
File-Based Routing in app/

Next.js App Router uses the filesystem as the router. Each folder under app/ becomes a URL segment. Special files define the UI for each segment.

  • page.tsx — the unique UI for that route (makes the route public)
  • layout.tsx — shared UI wrapping children; persists across navigations
  • loading.tsx — Suspense fallback shown while page loads
  • error.tsx — error boundary for the segment
  • not-found.tsx — shown when notFound() is called
app/
  layout.tsx          → root layout (html, body)
  page.tsx            → /
  about/
    page.tsx          → /about
  blog/
    layout.tsx        → shared blog layout
    page.tsx          → /blog
    [slug]/
      page.tsx        → /blog/my-post (dynamic segment)
  (marketing)/        → route group (no URL segment)
    landing/
      page.tsx        → /landing

Nested Layouts

Layouts nest by default. The root layout wraps everything. A route's layout wraps only its segment and children — it doesn't re-render on child navigation.

theory.title: Server vs Client Components
theory.content:
Server Components (Default)

All components in app/ are Server Components by default. They render on the server, sending HTML to the client with zero JavaScript for the component itself.

  • Can async/await directly — fetch data, read files, access DB
  • Cannot use browser APIs, useState, useEffect, or event listeners
  • Smaller client bundle — component code never shipped to browser
// app/users/page.tsx — Server Component
export default async function UsersPage() {
  // Direct DB or API call — no useEffect needed
  const users = await db.user.findMany();
  return (
    
    
      {users.map(u => 
  • {u.name}
    • )}
    

  );
}

Client Components

Add 'use client' at the top to opt into browser rendering. Required for interactivity, hooks, and browser APIs.

'use client';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return ;
}

Composition Pattern

Keep Server Components as high as possible. Pass interactive islands as children or props to minimise the client boundary:

// Server Component wrapping a Client Component
export default async function Page() {
  const data = await fetchData(); // server-side
  return ; // client gets data as prop
}

theory.title: Rendering Strategies
theory.content:
Static Rendering (Default)

Pages are rendered at build time and cached as static HTML. Fastest possible delivery via CDN. A page is static unless it opts into dynamic rendering.

// Statically rendered — no dynamic data sources
export default async function AboutPage() {
  return 
About Us
;
}

// Force static even with dynamic-looking fetch
export const dynamic = 'force-static';

Dynamic Rendering

A page renders on every request when it uses dynamic data sources: cookies(), headers(), searchParams, or a fetch with no-store.

export default async function Dashboard({ searchParams }) {
  // searchParams makes this dynamic automatically
  const data = await fetch('/api/data', { cache: 'no-store' });
  return ;
}

Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR)

Regenerate a static page in the background after a specified interval. Stale content served immediately; fresh version generated and cached.

// Revalidate every 60 seconds
export const revalidate = 60;

// Or per-fetch
const data = await fetch('/api/posts', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } });

// On-demand revalidation
import { revalidatePath, revalidateTag } from 'next/cache';
revalidatePath('/blog');       // invalidate a specific path
revalidateTag('posts');        // invalidate all fetches tagged 'posts'

theory.title: Data Fetching & Caching
theory.content:
fetch() in Server Components

Next.js extends the native fetch API with caching and revalidation options. Multiple components can fetch the same URL — Next.js deduplicates the request within one render.

// Default: cached until manually invalidated (like static)
const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/posts');

// Always fresh: opt out of caching
const data = await fetch('/api/live', { cache: 'no-store' });

// Time-based revalidation
const data = await fetch('/api/products', {
  next: { revalidate: 3600 } // fresh every hour
});

// Tag-based revalidation
const data = await fetch('/api/posts', {
  next: { tags: ['posts'] }
});

React cache()

For non-fetch data sources (ORMs, SDKs), use React's cache() to deduplicate within a single render:

import { cache } from 'react';

export const getUser = cache(async (id: string) => {
  return db.user.findUnique({ where: { id } }); // called at most once per id per render
});

Parallel Data Fetching

// BAD — sequential (waterfall)
const user = await getUser(id);
const posts = await getPostsByUser(user.id);

// GOOD — parallel
const [user, posts] = await Promise.all([
  getUser(id),
  getPostsByUser(id),
]);

theory.title: Server Actions
theory.content:
What Are Server Actions?

Server Actions are async functions marked with 'use server'. They run on the server but can be called directly from client components or HTML forms — no separate API route needed.

// app/actions.ts
'use server';
import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache';

export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
  const title = formData.get('title') as string;
  const body = formData.get('body') as string;

  await db.post.create({ data: { title, body } });
  revalidatePath('/blog'); // invalidate cached blog page
}

theory.title: Routing & Navigation
theory.content:
Dynamic Segments

app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx        → /blog/hello-world
app/shop/[...path]/page.tsx     → /shop/a/b/c (catch-all)
app/[[...path]]/page.tsx        → / and /a/b/c (optional catch-all)

// Access params in page
export default async function BlogPost({ params }: { params: { slug: string } }) {
  const post = await getPost(params.slug);
  return 
{post.content}
;
}

// Generate static paths at build time
export async function generateStaticParams() {
  const posts = await getPosts();
  return posts.map(p => ({ slug: p.slug }));
}

Link & Programmatic Navigation

import Link from 'next/link';
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'; // client only

// Declarative
About

// Programmatic (Client Component)
const router = useRouter();
router.push('/dashboard');
router.replace('/login'); // no history entry
router.back();

Middleware

// middleware.ts (runs at the edge before every request)
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server';

export function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
  const token = request.cookies.get('auth-token');
  if (!token && request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith('/dashboard')) {
    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', request.url));
  }
  return NextResponse.next();
}

export const config = { matcher: ['/dashboard/:path*'] };

theory.title: Performance Optimization
theory.content:
Image Optimization

The next/image component automatically optimises images: resizes, converts to WebP/AVIF, and lazy-loads.

import Image from 'next/image';

// Optimised — specify width/height to prevent layout shift


// Remote images need domain in next.config.ts
images: { remotePatterns: [{ hostname: 'images.unsplash.com' }] }

Font Optimization

import { Inter, Fira_Code } from 'next/font/google';

// Self-hosted at build time — no runtime request to Google Fonts
const inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'], variable: '--font-inter' });

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return {children};
}

Lazy Loading

import dynamic from 'next/dynamic';

// Heavy component loaded only when rendered
const RichTextEditor = dynamic(() => import('./RichTextEditor'), {
  loading: () => 
Loading editor...
,
  ssr: false, // skip server render (browser-only libs)
});

Bundle Analysis

  enabled: process.env.ANALYZE === 'true',
